section_1.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept
section_1.content: Define a matrix as a function (transformation). A square matrix (n x n) maps a space to itself, but non-square matrices (m x n) represent a bridge between spaces of different dimensions (e.g., R^n to R^m).
section_1.example: Visualizing a 2D plane (flat sheet) and a 3D space (room). A matrix acts as the 'instructions' to move from one to the other.

section_2.title: Case 1: Dimensional Expansion (Tall Matrices)
section_2.content: Explain m > n matrices. These embed lower-dimensional objects into higher-dimensional spaces. The transformation creates a 'subspace' within the larger target dimension.
section_2.example: A 2D 'stick-figure' character drawn on a flat screen (R^2) being projected into a 3D hologram (R^3) using a 3x2 matrix.

section_3.title: Case 2: Dimensional Compression (Wide Matrices)
section_3.content: Explain n > m matrices. These collapse higher-dimensional information into a lower dimension. Emphasize the concept of 'Projection' and the loss of information (Kernel/Null space).
section_3.example: A 3D robotic arm's position (x, y, z) being tracked by a 2D security camera sensor (u, v) using a 2x3 matrix, essentially 'flattening' the 3D movement onto a 2D image plane.

section_4.title: Visual Synthesis & Summary
section_4.content: Synthesize the two cases: Transformation = Mapping. Tall matrices 'unfold' or 'embed'; Wide matrices 'flatten' or 'project'.
section_4.example: Show an animation of a 3D cube collapsing into a 2D shadow (wide matrix) and a 2D drawing expanding into a 3D wireframe model (tall matrix) simultaneously on screen.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
